description: capture records: escape as the identity, entry selection by static reference kind, and the record as the first resolution tier for an applied value

cases.description: escape is idempotent: a value passed through another scope is unchanged
cases.comment: Capture happens at creation; there is no separate escape step. A value that leaves its defining scope already carries its record, so passing it through another function is the identity on it.

cases.description: a member both called and taken as a value contributes a value entry, not an open body
cases.comment: Any value-position reference forces the order edge, so the sibling's value exists and is captured — carrying its own record — and call-position resolution applies that captured value. Open-body entries appear only for members reached exclusively through call-position references, so record shapes depend only on static reference kinds.

cases.description: an applied value's record resolves before module entries
cases.comment: The record is the capture component of the parameters-and-captures tier, so the captured local wins over the same-named module function where the value is applied.

cases.description: a record member applied by name resolves group siblings through the same containing record
cases.comment: The record is one flat, mutually recursive binding group: the member's own body resolves names through the containing record before module entries, so the group sibling wins over the same-named module function.

cases.description: an applied value's record resolves before builtins
cases.comment: The captured local function shadows the builtin of the same name when the escaped value is applied.
